main_text.p: bonus καὶ φιλανθρωπος[?] optimo confilio de creuit, fieri. iuxta hæc dicta: Matth.20.22. Nescitis quid petatis. Rom.8.26. Quid enim precemur ut oportet, nō nouimus. sed ipfe Spiritus interpellat pro nobis gemitibus inenarrabilibus. Iacobi 4.3. Petitis, & nō accipitis, eo quòd male petatis, ut in uoluptates ueftras infumatis. Sedenim thefi κεφαλαιωδῶς[?] præmiffa, hypothefin de Iona propheta poftea tractabimus.

1. Eft è re hominis pij, trifticiq; fpiritu laborantis, fi ad Deum Patrem clementiffimum conuerfus, preces fundat. Vt maximè enim is filios fuos, ferulæ paternæ fubiectos, acerbiffimo doloris alicuius fenfu adfici & tentari patiatur:tamē nunquam paternæ φιλοστοργίας[?] obliuiscitur, ac proinde gratiam illius implorantes benignissimè exaudit.

2. Sed tamē à precibus longè abesse debet, expostulatio cum Deo, defensio antegressæ offensæ, siniftra de nimia indulgentia Dei opinio, & petitio pugnans cum uoluntate diuina. page.notes: Greek words are uncertain at several points and are marked [?]: the word after "bonus" (καὶ φιλανθρωπος), "κεφαλαιωδῶς" and "φιλοστοργίας". "dáda" is marked [?] because the accent is hard to read. The word "nunquam" is split across a line end without a printed hyphen and is written whole. "gemitibus" is also split without a printed hyphen and is written whole. The catchword "men-" is at the lower right below the last line. The page shows no damage, stamps or margin notes.
